Subject: Follow-up from demo + MAP kickoff (technical scope)

Karthik / team — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap from our side and a request to get a Mutual Action Plan started so we can align timelines internally.

Recap / goals:
- HealthGrid will run a short technical evaluation to validate latency and per-token cost for our core lab-assistant workflow (avg. prompt+response length ~400 tokens).
- Success criteria we discussed: 95th percentile latency <= 350ms for single-stream inference; end-to-end throughput target of ~25 reqs/min sustained for peak traffic (for initial test cohort). Cost target: <= $0.00045/token for production-like batching.

Dependencies we need from Redwood to start:
- A short MAP draft that lists milestones, owner on each side, target close date for the POC, and what infra/access you need from us (e.g., S3 access, test corpus, VPN/VPC peering info).
- A benchmark spec / script we can run (or Redwood-run option) and a short model shortlist you recommend for the tradeoff space (latency vs. quality).

Our internal timeline: wed like a POC kickoff next week (w/c Oct 11) and target a final evaluation readout by Oct 29 so procurement can review in the following cycle. If that looks like a hard deadline for Redwood, flag it.

Attaching the internal evaluation rubric we discussed (summary). Please also include any compliance items we should surface to security/compliance early (SOC2 evidence, data retention options).

Thanks — Emma
Emma Jones
Head of ML, HealthGrid

Subject: Re: MAP draft: technical evaluation roadmap & acceptance criteria (HealthGrid)

Emma / team — adding more detail on the benchmark spec and a pragmatic model shortlist for the POC. I kept the runs small so we can iterate quickly.

Benchmark notes / methodology:
- Canonical test corpus: 10k de-duplicated prompts (HealthGrid will provide subsample via S3).
- Measurement windows: warm (first 200 requests) and steady-state (next 10k). Report p50/p95/p99 latency, memory footprint, and GPU utilization. Report token-level cost computed from Redwood billing model + batch sizes used.
- Run modes: single-stream (latency-focused) and batched throughput (efficiency-focused) with 8/16/32 micro-batches to estimate scaling.

Initial model shortlist (recommended for tradeoff exploration):
- Llama-2-Chat-13B (quantized variant) — baseline for quality vs latency
- Mistral-7B-instruct — low-latency candidate for cost efficiency
- RedInfer-v1 (Redwood-verified tuned variant) — high-quality / mid-latency candidate
- Fallback: small instruction-tuned 3B model for failover and cost testing

Target run instances (examples): gpus with A10G or H100 depending on model — well pick exact instance and quantization profile in the spec.

Acceptance thresholds (concrete numbers to start):
- 95p latency <= 350ms (single-stream)
- End-to-end test cost <= $0.00045/token (measured with the same batching config used in production)
- Throughput test: stable 25 reqs/min across 5-minute windows for the sample cohort during batched mode

Ill attach a short benchmark checklist and a script stub that can either be run by HealthGrid or executed by Redwood if you prefer. Also happy to run the first set of tests on our side to minimize your ops lift.

Thanks — Ben
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
